name: EU reference implementations, registry, consortium architectures and pilots
scope_note: Covers the EU-funded and EU-adjacent reference work on the DPP system: CIRPASS (2022-2024) D3.2 system architecture; CIRPASS-2 (2024-2027) D4.1 reference architecture and its Apache-2.0 open source test environment (mock EU registry, validator, data extractor, renderer, deploy resources, ontologies); the EU DPP registry as set up by Regulation (EU) 2024/1781 Art. 13-15 and Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1778, and its user guide for economic operators; the Battery Pass consortium (Technical Guidance v1.0, data model v1.2.0) and its successor BatteryPass-Ready (data model v2.0/v2.0.1, user stories v1.0, test environment); the Cir4Fun SDKs; the Eclipse OSS4DPP initiative; and three adjacent items classified as adjacent, not as EU reference implementations: TRACE4EU (Digital Europe, EBSI), DaCapo (Horizon Europe, AAS plus dataspace) and the commercial OpenDPP interop kit. It extends and corrects docs/research/gap-assessment-2026-10-15.md section 7.2 with dates; it does not repeat its rows. It leaves out GS1 resolver, AAS/IDTA, UNTP/W3C VC, Catena-X and EPCIS details, which other method files cover. Protected standards (EN 18216-18246, IEC 63278, IEC 61406, ISO/IEC 15459, ISO/IEC 18004, DIN DKE SPEC 99100) appear only as bibliographic references in 'specs' through their catalogue/sources.yaml ids; those catalogue records were not re-read in this session and are therefore not listed in 'sources'. No live system, registry, test environment, resolver or dataspace endpoint was contacted.
summary: The EU reference family splits the DPP system into a central EU layer and a decentralised operator layer. The central layer is the Commission-run DPP registry (operational since 2026-07-20 per the prior catalogue record ec-dpp-batteries-webpage-and-timeline, not re-read here; Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1778 in force 2026-08-06): a verified economic operator registers a URL-form unique product identifier (UPI) through a web form, a JSON/XML file upload of up to 100 records, or an API, and receives a unique registration identifier; the registry runs automated checks (semantic conformity, mandatory-data coherence, granularity, commodity code range, back-up link), stores identifiers, commodity code, service-provider reference and registrant data, and can issue a QSeal-sealed, timestamped proof of registration. Customs will verify the registration identifier and commodity code through an interconnection with EU CSW-CERTEX that must be operational within four years. The passport data itself stays with the economic operator or a DPP service provider, with a mandatory back-up copy at an independent provider (ESPR Art. 10(4), Art. 11(c)). CIRPASS D3.2 (2024) proposed two architectures for this split: an HTTP-URI design with an operator-controlled resolver, typed links and a default EU resolver of last resort, and a DID/VC design. CIRPASS-2 D4.1 v1.1 (2026-06) recommends JSON-LD as default exchange format, content negotiation (application/ld+json versus application/vc+jwt), DPPs and updates as W3C VCs with JOSE enveloping proofs (ES256 first), hash-chained immutable updates with signed receipts, Bitstring Status List, generic roles carried as SD-JWT VCs under eIDAS 2.0, UPI-to-URI redirection with an EU fallback, a /.well-known model-level endpoint and a central search-key repository. The CIRPASS-2 test environment prototypes the registry and web portal: a Quarkus mock registry (JSON Schema 2020-12 metadata, liveURL/backupURL pointers, SHA-256 hash of the fetched DPP, RS256 proof-of-registration JWT, optional detached JWS on submissions), a validator that auto-selects JSON Schema or SHACL, an extractor that polls the registry and indexes search keys from JSON, JSON-LD, RDF or AAS JSON, and a renderer that fetches the live URL with content negotiation and compares DPPs via SPARQL-backed paths, all behind Keycloak OIDC with roles admin/eo/eu. Its battery ontology publishes OWL modules plus SHACL shapes and three access-tier views. Battery Pass (concluded April 2025) contributed an RDF/SAMM data model with generated JSON Schema, JSON-LD, AASX and OpenAPI artefacts and a Technical Guidance that splits EC central services, distributed operator services and third-party backup services; its successor BatteryPass-Ready ships JSON Schema 2020-12 and XSD per battery category and runs a validation test environment. End to end: the operator assigns a UPI and encodes it in the carrier, hosts the DPP (and a back-up), registers the UPI in the EU registry, and users reach the DPP by resolving the carrier URL with content negotiation and role-based access.

maturity.adoption_evidence: The EU registry is in production (registry.product-passport.ec.europa.eu, per the user guide) with a separate acceptance test site, but the guide states that successful battery registration is not yet possible. CIRPASS-2 lists 49 consortium partners and pilots in textiles, electronics, construction and automotive/tyres (test environment report); its tools are packaged as GHCR images and a single Docker Compose stack, with no hosted public instance documented. Battery Pass ran a demonstrator (WP4 documents in the repository) and BatteryPass-Ready announced a public test environment (resources page). Cir4Fun SDKs are on PyPI and in a Maven monorepo but have no GitHub releases. OpenDPP runs a hosted commercial node. TRACE4EU published EUPL-1.2 components (2024-11 to 2025-07). No independent adoption metrics were located.
maturity.regulatory_alignment: The registry, customs link and back-up obligations are set by law: ESPR Art. 13(1)-(6) (registry stores at least the unique identifiers, the commodity code for products released for free circulation and battery identifiers; operator uploads; registry returns a registration identifier; authorities have access), Art. 14 (public web portal searchable within access rights), Art. 15 (customs verify registration identifier and commodity code; EU CSW-CERTEX interconnection within four years of the Art. 13(5) implementing act), Art. 10(1) and 10(4), Art. 11(a)-(h); Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 Art. 77(2) three access groups, Art. 77(7)-(8) new linked passport after reuse/repurposing/remanufacturing and end after recycling, Art. 77(10) upload of the battery identifier to the ESPR registry, Art. 78(a)-(h); Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1778 Art. 3, 4-6a, 7, 8-15, 17-22. CIRPASS, CIRPASS-2, Battery Pass and BatteryPass-Ready outputs interpret these provisions and add design choices (JSON-LD default, VC-JOSE, hash chains, receipts, fallback resolver, /.well-known endpoint, search-key repository) that the law does not require.

L01_unique_identifiers.mechanism: EU registry: the UPI is a mandatory URL-form value supplied by the operator, https only, at most 2000 characters; optional Model Identifier and Batch Identifier fields at item level; the registry returns a Unique Registration Identifier (the guide abbreviates it 'URI', which clashes with RFC 3986 usage) after successful checks (guide 6.2.1 and glossary; 2026/1778 Art. 8(8),(10); ESPR Art. 13(5)). Item-level records link batch and model identifiers where they exist (2026/1778 Art. 8(4)-(5)). Mock registry: free-string 'upi' 1-200 characters (examples urn:epc:id:sgtin:0614141.107346.2017), 'reoId' 1-50 characters (examples LEI-..., EORI-...), 'facilitiesId' array of strings up to 250 characters (examples GLN-...), registry-generated 'registryId' (36-character UUID), 'modelUpi'/'batchUpi' cross-references; field names configurable (registry.upi-field-name, registry.reoid-field-name); reoId can be taken from a JWT claim instead of the payload. CIRPASS D3.2: Product UID as a canonical HTTP URI (with a UID-to-URI transformation for legacy numbers, GS1 Digital Link given as the main example) or a DID variant where the product DID is the REO DID plus a query part with a UUID (did:method:REO-DID?UUID=...). D4.1: operator-run UPI-to-URI redirection (3.16) with an EU fallback redirection service (3.17); item-level UPIs for products expecting lifecycle events (3.20); facility identifiers issued by trusted bodies. Battery Pass v1.2.0: SAMM properties productIdentifier and batteryPassportIdentifier in urn:samm:io.BatteryPass.GeneralProductInformation:1.2.0#. TRACE4EU: did:ebsi actor identifiers and a did:web issuer (did:web:trace4eu.github.io:trace4eu-dpp-interop-did-web). OpenDPP: GS1 Digital Link paths /01/{gtin}, /01/{gtin}/21/{serial}, /8003/{grai}.

L01_unique_identifiers.observable_black_box: The UPI string decoded from the carrier; whether it is an https URL of at most 2000 characters; whether it dereferences; the registration identifier returned by a registry; consistency of upi/modelUpi/batchUpi across registry record and passport.
L01_unique_identifiers.law_delta: ESPR requires a persistent UPI connected through a carrier and registry identifiers; the user guide adds the URL-form and https-only rule and the 2000-character limit, and says the UPI must follow JTC 24 standards (guide's wording; standard content not read). The mock registry is looser than the EU registry: it accepts non-URL URNs and 200 characters.

L02_data_carriers.mechanism: Carrier content is the UPI only (CIRPASS D3.2 3.1.6 recommends carrying just the product-UID URI). Battery carriers are QR codes linked to the unique identifier (Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 Art. 77(3)); ESPR Art. 10(1)(b) requires physical presence on product, packaging or documentation and Art. 10(3) a digital copy for dealers and marketplaces within five working days. D4.1 3.19 recommends a separate model-level carrier or link for online and pre-purchase use, not a second carrier on the product. The CIRPASS-2 renderer front end has a camera QR scanner that hands the decoded URL to the fetch flow; the CIRPASS-2 CORE ontology deliberately excludes carriers (ontologies-core issue 61, as reported in the battery README). Battery Pass Technical Guidance 6.1 discusses QR, RFID, NFC and Data Matrix options (its summaries of ISO/IEC carrier standards are not recorded here).

L03_data_exchange_protocols.mechanism: HTTP content negotiation on one URL is the shared assumption. CIRPASS-2 test environment design assumption 3.1: the live URL (in the registry or the QR code) returns HTML to a browser without a specific Accept header and machine-readable DPP data for Accept application/json or application/ld+json; POST and custom headers are excluded because a QR URL cannot carry them. The renderer back end sends all supported media types in Accept, routes by returned Content-Type, returns plain JSON as is, expands JSON-LD, and converts Turtle, RDF/XML, N-Triples, N3 and N-Quads to expanded JSON-LD with Apache Jena. The mock registry fetches the liveURL with Accept application/json or application/ld+json before validation and hashing. D4.1 3.1: application/ld+json returns the JSON-LD DPP; application/vc+jwt returns the full DPP as a JOSE-enveloped VC (compact JWS whose payload is the compacted JSON-LD DPP, header cty vc). CIRPASS D3.2: the product URI points to an REO resolver that answers with RFC 9110 redirects; a plain GET yields the consumer HTML view; role- or format-specific targets are selected with typed links (RFC 8288), a linkset (RFC 9264) lists available link types; resolvers can chain; a default EU resolver answers when the REO host is gone. EU registry: the registry itself dereferences the submitted UPI and rejects excessive redirects, redirects to a less secure protocol, disallowed domains or ports and oversized responses (guide 6.2.2 error list). Battery Pass TG 4.6: HTTPS over TCP/IP, REST, JSON-LD payloads, a translator service mapping generic CRUD calls to platform-specific APIs, GraphQL in the demonstrator, co-existing standard APIs (AAS, NGSI-LD, Web of Things, EPCIS) and dataspace connectors (Eclipse Dataspace Components, FIWARE connector). Cir4Fun: generated EDC client. TRACE4EU: OID4VCI pre-authorised code flow for credential issuance. OpenDPP: GET /passport/{id} with Accept application/aas+json, application/vc+jwt or vc+ld+json.

(Produces application/jwt; 404 if unknown); POST /schema/v1, GET /schema/v1/current, DELETE /schema/v1/current; GET /q/openapi (JSON or YAML by Accept, generated from the active schema); GET /.well-known/jwks.json. There is no GET or search endpoint for registry records in the code (the report says the registry exposes a search API; see anomalies). Validator: POST /validate/v1 (auto-match), POST /validate/v1/{name}/{version}; POST /resource/v1/{payloadType} multipart (payloadType json, json_ld, turtle, rdf_xml, rdf_json, n3, n_triples, n_quads); GET/DELETE /resource/v1/{resourceType}/{id}; codes 200, 204, 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 500. Extractor: GET /capabilities/v1, POST /config/v1, GET and DELETE /config/v1/current. Renderer back end: GET /fetch/v1?url=..., POST /search/v1 with filters [{property, op in EQ|LT|LTE|GT|GTE|LIKE, literal}], offset, limit (AND-combined; string literals in single quotes), POST /comparison/v1 with dppUrls and propertyPaths in the form segment[*@type=Type].property per namespace. EU registry (2026/1778 Art. 3(a)-(b), Art. 8(6)): secure web interface and API; the user guide documents the web form (single DPP) and file upload (JSON or XML, max 100 DPPs, max 1 GB, template per format, all-or-nothing rejection), a correlation ID, statuses PROCESSING, SUCCESS, FAILURE, per-DPP error details and CSV export; the API itself is not documented publicly. Cir4Fun SDK routes (project-defined): /v1/dpps and /v1/dpps/{dppId} (create, full or compressed read, update, delete), /v1/dppsByProductId/{productId}, /v1/dppsByIdAndDate/{dppId}?date={instant} (historical read), POST /v1/dppsByProductIds (batch lookup), /v1/dpps/{dppId}/elements/{elementIdPath} (fine-grained read and update using a singular subset of RFC 9535 JSONPath; partial update follows RFC 7396 merge semantics but is sent as application/json), POST /v1/registerDPP (registry registration with metadata only); mock returns 400 for malformed paths, 404 for no node, 501 for unsupported. Battery Pass TG 4.4: core services onboarding, issuing (bulk and single), update, transfer, archiving, search/view/compare; WSDL/OpenAPI for definitions; SPARQL for querying. BatteryPass-Ready user stories: seven modules (authentication and authorisation, registration, create DPP, read (QR public read or controlled read), update, backup, deletion). Search: ESPR Art. 14 web portal; D4.1 3.23 central search-key repository; CIRPASS-2 extractor indexes model-level entries only.

L05_system_interoperability_data_models.mechanism: CIRPASS-2 CORE ontology (EU DPP CO; modules P_DPP v2.1.0, MAT v1.1.0, published on the DPP Vocabulary Hub) plus sector modules. Battery modules (umbrella 0.4.0 DRAFT) use namespaces https://w3id.org/eudpp/battery#, battery-performance#, battery-materials#, battery-locations#, battery-chemistries#, battery-metals#, battery-labeling#, battery-extinguisher-classes#, battery-categories#, battery-statuses#, battery-cf-shapes#; no owl:imports, CORE terms referenced by IRI; no OWL cardinalities; mandatory/optional rules and access tiers expressed in SHACL (battery-shapes.ttl profile, three view files, battery-access-tiers.ttl) with a tests/run_tests.py harness (27 checks reported on 28 September, 23 here and 29 with fixtures on 6 October). Passport status values on dpp:dppStatus: Active, Archived, Inactive, Invalid; battery status (original, repurposed, re-used, remanufactured, waste) on bat:hasBatteryStatus. TalTech namespaces http://dpp.taltech.ee/EUDPP# (reference ontology) and http://dpp.taltech.ee/MODDPP# appear in extractor and renderer configuration. Validator: JSON payloads matched to a schema by weighted Jaccard similarity over required property paths (variants from oneOf/anyOf/allOf, pattern properties); JSON-LD payloads matched to SHACL templates by root @type against owl:targetClass, then @context URI, then vocabulary URI; templates accepted in Turtle, RDF/XML, JSON-LD, N-Triples, N-Quads, N3. Extractor strategies in fixed order: AAS JSON (root modelType AssetAdministrationShellEnvironment, Submodel or AssetAdministrationShell; semanticId suffix-insensitive match, then idShortPath; MultiLanguageProperty by preferLanguage), known ontology (exact key paths with @type filters), unknown-ontology JSON-LD (typeHints plus variants), plain JSON (case-insensitive variants with parent-context rules); target types STRING or DECIMAL. Mock registry metadata: JSON Schema draft 2020-12, properties limited to primitives or arrays of primitives. EU registry: semantic repository with meanings, link specifications, data models and formats, role meanings, multilingual labels, DCAT-AP metadata and a free public search API (2026/1778 Art. 11-12); registration files are JSON or XML following pre-defined schemas with downloadable templates (guide). D4.1: JSON-LD default (other formats optional), compacted form inside VCs, versioned @context URLs kept available for the DPP lifetime, templates as JSON Schema plus SHACL describing source, product group, granularity, cardinality, units, semantic identifier, access rights, proof needs, update rules and version per element. Battery Pass v1.2.0: platform-independent RDF model in SAMM 2.1.0 (urn:samm:io.BatteryPass.<Aspect>:<version>#) with seven aspects (GeneralProductInformation, CarbonFootprint, Circularity, Labels, MaterialComposition, Performance 1.2.1, SupplyChainDueDiligence) and generated JSON Schema, JSON-LD, payload JSON, AAS/AASX, OpenAPI 3.0, AsyncAPI, SQL, HTML; aligned to DIN DKE SPEC 99100:2025-02 per README (bibliographic only). BatteryPass-Ready v2.x: JSON Schema 2020-12 and XSD (v1.3 and v2.0) per category (EV, industrial without BMS, LMT, other industrial above 2 kWh, stationary above 2 kWh), each with a 'Feb27' variant; no mandatory requirements at master level; twelve conditional elements left optional pending plausibility checks; no SAMM, JSON-LD or SHACL. OpenDPP kit vendors the CIRPASS-2 registry schema verbatim, an AAS v3 schema, UNTP DPP 0.7.0 schema and EPCIS 2.0.1 schema.

L06_storage_archiving_persistence.mechanism: Passport data is stored by the responsible operator or a DPP service provider (ESPR Art. 11(c); Batteries Art. 78(c)), with a back-up copy at a service provider (ESPR Art. 10(4)) and availability after insolvency or cessation (ESPR Art. 11(e); Batteries Art. 78(e)). The mock registry stores liveURL and backupURL (both required, pattern ^http) and the SHA-256 and content type of the fetched live DPP. CIRPASS D3.2: decentralised DPP data repositories (knowledge graphs, SPARQL endpoints), archives as a cheaper, slower last resort reached through a root (default EU) resolver; long-term archives may strip data. D4.1 3.15: the back-up provider holds all data including optional data, keeps it current and enforces the same access rules; it can attest a successor operator; 3.21 caching for bulk users with the operator as source of truth. Battery Pass TG 4.7 and 5.3: high-availability storage, archiving by a third-party provider, back-ups in the platform-independent semantic format rather than system-specific formats. BatteryPass-Ready: backup module after every registration or update and soft deletion at the backup service provider. Registry side (2026/1778): registration data deleted 10 years after registration unless Union law sets another period (Art. 10(3)); logs kept six months (access), five years (administrative, data exchange) or registration lifetime (modifications) (Art. 14(3)); availability at all times except maintenance, outage records kept five years (Art. 15). TRACE4EU off-chain storage: Apache Cassandra behind an OIDC-protected proxy with scopes ocs:read and ocs:write.

L07_access_rights_security_confidentiali.mechanism: Law: battery access groups are the public; notified bodies, market surveillance authorities and the Commission; persons with a legitimate interest (Batteries Art. 77(2)), detailed by the Art. 77(9) implementing act (not located); ESPR Art. 11(b) free access by role and Art. 11(f) restricted write rights. EU registry: users authenticate with EU Login (MFA); organisations are verified by an EC-sealed PDF declaration counter-signed or sealed with a QES or QSeal from a QTSP (guide 4); 2026/1778 Art. 4-5 accept QES, eID at assurance level high or (qualified) electronic attestations of attributes, verified status valid up to three years, Art. 6 delegation to third-party users, Art. 7 designated national administrators by 2027-02-18. Registration (Art. 8): by a verified operator (or verified third party) at the granularity set by the delegated act or Union law, the most granular level winning when several apply; automated checks of semantic conformity, mandatory-data coherence, granularity, commodity-code validity against permitted ranges and back-up link; unique persistent registration identifier returned in the interface or API response; stored data: unique identifiers, commodity codes, service-provider references, registrant information including registration time and passport integrity. Art. 6a transfer of passports to another verified operator; Art. 10 logging and versioning with Commission timestamps; Art. 21(3) sharing with authorities including customs. User guide: production at https://registry.product-passport.ec.europa.eu/, acceptance test site at registry.acc.product-passport.ec.europa.eu (printed with http://, separate EU Login, periodic data cleaning, same verification as production); product group 'Batteries' pre-selected, item level only; registration record vs DPP data distinction. end_to_end_flows.name: EU registry registration by a verified operator (production rules)
steps: 1. User signs in through EU Login (MFA) at the registry web site.
2. User enrols the organisation; the registry produces an EC-sealed PDF declaration of the entered data.

3. Legal representative signs or seals the PDF with a QES or QSeal from a QTSP and uploads it; the registry checks file, signature, certificates and data, and marks the organisation verified (user becomes organisation administrator).
4. Operator hosts the DPP data and makes the https UPI resolve to it.
5. Operator registers one DPP by web form (UPI, optional model and batch identifiers) or up to 100 DPPs by JSON or XML file; a correlation ID is returned.
6. Registry validates schema, duplicates, UPI URL syntax, dereferences the UPI (redirect, protocol and size limits) and runs semantic validation; any error rejects the whole file.
7. Request moves from PROCESSING to SUCCESS (UPI, registration identifier, product group per DPP) or FAILURE (UPI, error per DPP, CSV export).
8. Operator can download a QSeal-sealed proof of registration with Commission timestamp and passport-version hash, valid for 90 days (2026/1778 Art. 9).

end_to_end_flows.name: CIRPASS-2 test environment: rEO registration
steps: 1. rEO system gets a JWT from Keycloak with the client-credentials grant; a protocol mapper adds reoId and reoName.

2. rEO POSTs JSON metadata (upi, reoId, liveURL, backupURL, commodityCode, facilitiesId, granularityLevel, ...) to /metadata/v1 or /metadata/v1/registerDPP, optionally with a detached RS256 JWS in x-jws-signature.
3. Registry validates the body against the active JSON Schema 2020-12.
4. Registry GETs the liveURL with Accept application/json or application/ld+json, stores sha256:<hex> and Content-Type, and if enabled forwards the payload to the validator.
5. On success the registry persists the record and answers 201 with registryId and the validation report; on validation failure 400 with the report.
6. rEO later GETs /metadata/v1/{registryId}/proof (application/jwt) and verifies it with /.well-known/jwks.json.

end_to_end_flows.name: CIRPASS-2 search-key extraction (background)
steps: 1. On a schedule (example every 30 s) the extractor reads model-level registry entries added or changed since the last run.
2. It GETs each liveURL with all supported Accept types.
3. It classifies the response (AAS JSON, known ontology, unknown-ontology JSON-LD, plain JSON) and applies the configured strategy.
4. It stores extracted fields keyed by UPI and live URL; failed entries get a retry counter and are dropped after max retrials.
5. GET /capabilities/v1 publishes the searchable fields used by the portal search form.

end_to_end_flows.name: CIRPASS-2 consumer visualisation (mock EU web portal)
steps: 1. User signs in (authorization code with PKCE).
2. User searches via POST /search/v1, enters a URL, or scans a QR code.
3. Back end GETs the live URL with content negotiation; JSON passes through; JSON-LD is expanded; other RDF serialisations are converted with Jena then expanded.
4. Front end renders with ontology-aware components for CIRPASS-2 CORE terms or a generic collapsible view.
5. Comparison: POST /comparison/v1 with type-filtered property paths per namespace, executed as SPARQL over each DPP.

end_to_end_flows.name: CIRPASS D3.2 HTTP flow with fallback
steps: 1. App decodes the product UID URI from the carrier (or transforms a non-URI UID into a URI).

2. Plain GET to the REO resolver returns a redirect to the consumer HTML view; a request carrying a link type gets the matching target (file or SPARQL endpoint); a linkset request lists all link types.
3. Privileged roles present credentials at the resolver/policy decision point; repairers write back with provenance data.
4. If the REO host is gone (no host or 404), the app asks the default EU resolver, fed by registry data, for a backup or archive target.

end_to_end_flows.name: Customs release (ESPR Art. 15, future)
steps: 1. Declarant provides the registration identifier with the customs declaration (applies since the registry is operational).

2. Customs verifies registration identifier and commodity code against the registry, electronically through EU CSW-CERTEX once the interconnection is operational (deadline four years after 2026-08-06).
3. Release for free circulation follows; it is not proof of compliance.

end_to_end_flows.name: Third-party update with receipt (D4.1 recommendation)
steps: 1. Repairer authenticates with a role credential and submits update content.
2. rEO system serialises concurrent updates, adds the hash of the previous version and signs the update as a VC.
3. rEO returns a signed receipt with a hash of the submitted content.
4. Update is mirrored to the back-up provider and optionally anchored with a trusted third party.

end_to_end_flows.name: BatteryPass-Ready module chain (EO via main service provider)
steps: 1. Authentication and authorisation of each actor.
2. Create DPP: EO transfers DPP data to the MSP, which hosts it.
3. Registration: IDs submitted to the EC registry; registration ID received.
4. Backup: copy created at the backup service provider.
5. Read: public QR read or controlled read after authentication; Update and Backup repeat on changes; Deletion removes public hosting, soft-deletes at the backup provider and notifies the registry.

end_to_end_flows.name: TRACE4EU credential-backed battery passport (adjacent)
steps: 1. Actors hold did:ebsi identities; legal entity identifiers are checked against the EBSI ledger.
2. Certification bodies and auditors issue VCs (carbon footprint, responsible mining, due diligence) via OID4VCI.
3. The manufacturer issues a battery passport credential whose subject is the battery serial number and references supplier credentials.
4. Verifiers check signatures and ledger anchors; confidential data sits in off-chain storage behind scoped tokens.

failure_modes.fault: Live URL ignores Accept and always returns HTML, so the registry cannot hash or validate data.
failure_modes.detectable_by: identifier.resolve with accept='application/ld+json' fails on text/html final media type.

failure_modes.fault: Server negotiates but omits 'Vary: Accept', so caches serve HTML to machines or JSON to browsers.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Inspect Vary on negotiated responses (needs the proposed negotiation matrix check).

failure_modes.fault: Redirect chain downgrades from https to http or loops.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Bounded resolution recording each hop; registry preflight check.

failure_modes.fault: UPI printed as an EPC URN or plain GTIN, which the EU registry rejects as an invalid URL.
Item-level record without modelUpi/batchUpi or batch record carrying batchUpi.
failure_modes.detectable_by: data.jsonschema against the mock registry schema.

failure_modes.fault: dppHash computed over a different representation or with formatting differences, so the hash never matches.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Recompute SHA-256 per media type and compare; the mock README example hash is itself only 63 hex digits without the 'sha256:' prefix.

failure_modes.fault: Proof JWT verifies only via a JWKS URL controlled by the same server (no independent trust anchor).
failure_modes.detectable_by: integrity.jws reports issuer-trust failure when the key is not in the pinned trust bundle.

failure_modes.fault: Detached JWS checked against a key fetched from a caller-supplied jwksUri claim, letting a caller pick its own trust root.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Submit a body signed by a key at an attacker-controlled JWKS (loopback) and observe acceptance.

failure_modes.fault: Role 'eu' labelled End User can upload or delete validation schemas and registry schemas (observed path policies).
failure_modes.detectable_by: Write-authorisation probes with an eu token expecting 403.

failure_modes.fault: backupURL points at the same host or at a GS1 resolver URL instead of an independent provider copy (as in the OpenDPP registry pointer sample).
failure_modes.detectable_by: Compare hosts and content of liveURL and backupURL.

failure_modes.fault: Conditional battery attributes missing because the consortium schemas make them optional.
failure_modes.detectable_by: data.rules completeness pack per battery category.

failure_modes.fault: Search-key cache truncates or rejects UPIs longer than 36 characters (extractor and renderer DDL declare upi VARCHAR(36) while the registry allows 200 and the EU registry 2000).
failure_modes.detectable_by: Register a long UPI in a loopback stack and search for it.

failure_modes.fault: Renderer fetch proxy (GET /fetch/v1?url=) fetches arbitrary URLs, including internal addresses.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Loopback probe with an internal-address URL; expect refusal.

failure_modes.fault: Duplicate registration silently overwrites the previous record (MODIFY default), losing history.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Register the same UPI twice and inspect history or registryId behaviour.

failure_modes.fault: Content-Type spelled 'application/json+ld' instead of 'application/ld+json' (appears in a mock README example).
File upload with one bad record rejects all records; operators misread partial success.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Not testable against the official registry; replicate in a mock with a recorded outcome fixture.

open_questions: Will the Commission publish the registry API specification ('DPP Registry technical guidelines' section still empty on 2026-10-19), and does the API registration payload match the JSON/XML upload templates?

Which exact hashing input does the EU registry use for the 'hash of the version of the digital product passport' (2026/1778 Art. 2 definition, Art. 9(2)(e)): bytes of a negotiated representation, a canonical form, or a value supplied by the operator?
What thresholds does the EU registry apply when it dereferences a UPI (redirect count, response size, allowed ports and domains)? The guide names the error classes only.
Does the mock 'eu' role mean End User (README) or EU authority (deploy-resources maps privileged CRUD to the public-authority client)? The answer changes which access tests are meaningful.
Is the CIRPASS-2 CORE ontology repository (ontologies-core) private, renamed or moved? Pinning SHACL fixtures needs the CORE files.

When will the battery semantic catalogue be defined so that battery registration succeeds (guide 6.2.1), and will it be exposed through the public semantic repository search API (2026/1778 Art. 12(5)-(7))?
Does the Battery Pass repository's CC BY 4.0 statement cover the deliverable PDFs in docs/, given the acatech imprint on thebatterypass.eu?
What did the OSS4DPP community meetings of 17 and 24 September 2026 decide about a conformance-testing project?
anomalies: User guide version labels disagree: PDF 'Last Published 2026-09-16 v1.03' versus resources page 'V3' dated 14 September 2026.
User guide prints the test environment as http://registry.acc.product-passport.ec.europa.eu/ (http, not https), while it requires https for UPIs.
User guide abbreviates Unique Registration Identifier as 'URI', colliding with the RFC 3986 meaning used elsewhere in the same family.

CIRPASS-2 test environment report says the Mock EU Registry exposes a search API; the code exposes only POST /metadata/v1(/registerDPP) and GET /metadata/v1/{registryId}/proof; search lives in renderer-be over the extractor cache.

mock-eu-registry README: one example returns contentType 'application/json+ld' while others use 'application/ld+json'; the first example dppHash has 63 hex digits (a mistyped SHA-256 of the empty string) and lacks the documented 'sha256:' prefix.
mock-eu-registry README uses config keys registry-auth.oidc.role-claim-path and registry.oidc.role-claim-path in examples, while the configuration table lists quarkus.oidc.roles.role-claim-path.
dpp-data-extractor README links its artifacts to the mock-eu-registry releases page; dpp-renderer-be README Docker Compose examples deploy the extractor image (copy-paste errors).
Extractor and renderer DDL declare upi VARCHAR(36) although the registry schema allows UPIs up to 200 characters.
